reason: The hypothesis directly restates the core finding of P7 and P14 (nanoclustering of Cr, Ni, Mn at GBs causes embrittlement) and combines it with the well-known effect of strain rate on deformation-induced segregation from P1, P8, P9, and P10. The proposed test simply varies the strain rate to modulate the already-known segregation, which is a minor extension of the existing evidence rather than a new synthesis or transfer.
copied_elements: Intermediate-temperature embrittlement in single-phase CrMnFeCoNi HEA
Nanoclustering of Cr, Ni, and Mn at grain boundaries reduces cohesion and causes intergranular cracking
Ductility loss at intermediate temperatures is correlated with GB cracking
Deformation-induced dislocation movement enhances solute diffusion to grain boundaries
Strain rate affects segregation: lower strain rate allows more diffusion, higher strain rate suppresses it
